Here’s a more conversational version that sounds more natural while still protecting you and keeping the facts clear:

:::writing{variant="email" id="61427" subject="RE: Leave and Return to Work"}
Hi [HR Name],  

I just want to clarify that it was never communicated to me, verbally or in writing, that the third week of approved leave was contingent on me not taking my previously planned Mexico trip. I also don’t remember ever saying I had officially canceled it. What I remember saying was that I would probably have to cancel it depending on how recovery went.  

At the time of surgery, neither I nor my surgeons fully knew how extensive this recovery was going to be. Unfortunately, it has not gone textbook at all and has honestly been quite the opposite. As stated in the letter from my surgeon, I am currently under restrictions through May 19th, and I have an MRI scheduled next week that should hopefully give more answers and clarity on what’s going on and what the next steps look like.  

I also do not have any record or recollection of an agreement that I was indefinitely not going to Mexico in exchange for the approved leave. My understanding was simply that the organization approved three consecutive weeks off for surgery and recovery, which I appreciated.  

Right now, I’m still following my surgeon’s restrictions and recommendations. Until I get the MRI results and updated guidance next week, I really can’t responsibly confirm yet whether I’ll be cleared for regular duty by Monday’s office meeting or if restrictions will need to continue for a bit longer. I’ll absolutely keep you updated as soon as I know more.  

Thank you,  
Bethany
:::

Hi [HR Name],  

I want to clarify that it was never formally communicated to me, either verbally or in writing, that the third week of approved leave was contingent upon me not taking my previously planned trip to Mexico. I also do not recall ever stating that I had definitively canceled the trip. My recollection of the conversation was that I said I would probably have to cancel it depending on my recovery.  

At the time of surgery, neither I nor my medical team fully understood the extent or complexity of the recovery process. Unfortunately, my recovery has not followed a typical or “textbook” timeline and has been far more difficult than anticipated. As referenced in my physician’s documentation, I am currently under restrictions through May 19th, and I have an MRI scheduled next week which should provide additional clarity regarding my condition and next steps.  

I also do not have any record or recollection of an agreement stating that I would indefinitely forgo the trip in exchange for the approved leave. My understanding was simply that the organization approved three consecutive weeks of paid leave for surgery and recovery, which I appreciated.  

At this time, I am still following my physician’s restrictions and recommendations. Until I receive the MRI results and updated medical guidance next week, I cannot responsibly confirm whether I will be cleared to return to full regular duty by Monday’s office meeting or whether restrictions will need to continue temporarily. I will provide an update as soon as I have more definitive medical information.  

Thank you,  
Bethany
:::
